clue.text: This writer's put on fake leather

indicators.note: one piece is placed after the other, as if added on to it

parts.note: to fake something is to sham it; a sham is a fake
the setter speaking of themself: belonging to this writer is 'my'

explanation.surface: A writer confesses to passing off imitation leather as the real thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' reads as 'pretended', but here it says the writer's possessive is placed after the fake.
explanation.definitionFit: Shammy is a variant spelling of chamois, the soft leather used for polishing cars and windows.

clue.text: Thus short rope is needed in beauty parlours

parts.note: thus means so, as in 'and so it was'

indicators.note: short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a lariat is a cowboy's rope, a lasso

explanation.surface: A rope seems to be required equipment in salons, which is an odd picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Solaria are tanning rooms with sunlamps, a typical service in beauty salons.

clue.text: Lady troubled about first bit of knitwear that's polyester

indicators.note: about means going around, so the jumbled letters surround the next piece
troubled means disturbed, so the letters of the word lady are stirred up
the first bit of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A woman frets over her knitting, which turns out to be synthetic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges LADY to ALYD; 'about' puts K, from 'first bit of knitwear', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Alkyd is a type of polyester resin used in paints and coatings.

clue.text: The majority needing food to eat, being least contented

indicators.note: eating means taking something inside, so the first piece swallows the second

parts.note: the majority of things is most of them
a pie is an item of food

explanation.surface: Most people are unhappy because they need something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Mopey means glum and listless, so the mopiest person is the gloomiest and least satisfied.

clue.text: Misshaped model is shedding pounds to get a heavenly body

indicators.note: something misshaped has been bent out of form, so the letters are rearranged
shedding means casting off, so a letter must go from the fodder

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A deformed model is losing weight, apparently on the way to becoming a heavenly figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Take L out of MODELIS and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Deimos is the smaller of the two moons of Mars, a natural satellite.

clue.text: No longer having time, stop — or run on?

parts.note: ex means former, no longer the case
to stop is to end

explanation.surface: Out of time, someone wonders whether to finish or carry on.
explanation.definitionFit: To extend is to make something continue for longer, carry on beyond its limit.

clue.text: A comic ran about like 'Michelle, ma belle … '

indicators.note: about here means all around, in disorder, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A comedian dashes about singing a Beatles song.
explanation.walkthrough: The Beatles song 'Michelle' mixes English and French lyrics.
explanation.definitionFit: Macaronic verse mixes words from two languages, as that song blends English with French.

clue.text: Football broadcaster beginning to stultify listener

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a hearer is someone who listens

explanation.surface: A football pundit starts to bore the audience into a stupor.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Shearer is a former England striker who now works as a TV football pundit.
explanation.definitionFit: Alan Shearer is a well-known football commentator and pundit on British television.

clue.text: Copper interrupting nonsense in voting procedure that's shocking

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the combined piece goes into the next word

parts.note: an election is a procedure for voting

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so one piece goes into the middle of another

parts.note: rot is nonsense, rubbish
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A police officer barges into a ridiculous ballot, which is an outrage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interrupting' and 'in' are two nested insertions: the policeman's metal breaks into the nonsense, making ROCUT, and that whole piece then breaks into the voting word.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrocution is killing or injuring by electric shock, so it is literally shocking.

clue.text: Criticism not entirely crazy

indicators.note: not entirely means a word lacking its last letter

parts.note: flaky is informal for eccentric or crazy

explanation.surface: A piece of criticism that is only partly mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Flak is informal for strong adverse criticism, from anti-aircraft fire.

clue.text: Endless voting one expressed approval of — and tried to secure votes?

indicators.note: endless means losing the last letter

parts.note: a poll is a vote
I is the Roman numeral for one
ticking an item shows approval, as with a tick mark

explanation.surface: Someone approved of endless ballots and campaigned for support.
explanation.definitionFit: To politick is to engage in political campaigning, canvassing to win support.

clue.text: See 24
Like some urns (some terribly rare), nicked from the east

indicators.note: in an across clue, from the east means read from right to left
some of means only part of the words are used, the letters running across them

explanation.surface: A note on rare urns that were stolen from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nicked' looks like the hiding signal but is part of the hidden text; read YRARENIC backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinerary means relating to ashes, so cinerary urns hold the cremated remains of the dead.

clue.text: Femmes fatales near mates, misbehaving

indicators.note: misbehaving means acting wrongly, so the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Seductive women are behaving badly near their partners.
explanation.definitionFit: Man-eaters are women who pursue and use men, the role of a seductress.

clue.text: Unled soldiers overtake worker by the way

indicators.note: unled means without the lead, the first letter

parts.note: men are soldiers, as in officers and men
to pass a car is to overtake it
an ant is a worker, the classic crossword insect

explanation.surface: Leaderless troops overtake a labourer while passing along the road.
explanation.walkthrough: In chess en passant is also a capture by a pawn passing another, nicely echoing 'overtake'.
explanation.definitionFit: En passant is French for 'in passing', used to mean incidentally.

clue.text: Solitary person would be left with this single thing

indicators.note: the clue says the solitary person is formed by adding one letter, so taking that letter away leaves the solution
this refers to the answer, which joined with a letter makes the solitary person

parts.note: a loner is someone who keeps to themself

explanation.surface: A recluse would be left with just one thing.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as L plus the answer making LONER, so remove L from LONER.
explanation.definitionFit: A oner is British informal for something unique, one of a kind.

clue.text: Small drinks in vessels lacking height

indicators.note: lacking means without, so a letter is removed

parts.note: ships are vessels

explanation.surface: Little drinks served in short glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessels' suggests cups, but here it means boats.
explanation.definitionFit: Sips are tiny mouthfuls of a drink.

clue.text: Girl and dog jump

parts.note: Sal is a girl's name, short for Sally
a chow is a Chinese breed of dog

explanation.surface: A girl and her dog leap together.
explanation.definitionFit: A salchow is a figure-skating leap named after Ulrich Salchow.

clue.text: Twenty joining club maybe — a record at a sports ground

definitions.text: a record at a sports ground

parts.note: a score is twenty
a club is one example of a playing card

explanation.surface: Twenty people joining a sports club make a record at the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' suggests a sports club; it is the playing-card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A scorecard records the runs or points in a match, kept at cricket grounds and golf courses.

clue.text: Most peculiar 22 briefly wearing reddish-brown

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the colour is wrapped around the title

parts.note: rust is a reddish-brown colour
the French title at 22-across, shortened, is Mme

explanation.surface: An odd lady dressed in russet.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum is British informal for odd or strange, so rummest means strangest.

clue.text: Sheep's high-pitched noise, behaving violently

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep; the 's is a link
a ping is a short high ringing sound

explanation.surface: A sheep's shrill cry as it runs amok.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramping is an old sense of rearing up threateningly, raging, as in rampant.

clue.text: More than one boy that is attractive and healthy in Scotland

parts.note: boys are sons
i.e. is the abbreviation for 'that is', from Latin id est

explanation.surface: Several boys who are bonny and robust Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonsie is a Scots word for buxom, comely and healthy-looking.

clue.text: Elaborate situation created by streaker?

definitions.meaning: to elaborate on a plan is to fill in its details
a streaker runs naked, leaving bare skin on show

explanation.surface: Someone asks for details about the scene a naked runner causes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elaborate' is a verb here, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To expand a sketchy idea with details is a common phrasal verb; the second reading is skin uncovered.

clue.text: She's married numberless men, including an old gardener

indicators.note: including means holding inside, so the trimmed word surrounds the gardener
N is the abbreviation for number, so numberless removes that letter

parts.note: taken as written before losing a letter
Adam tended the Garden of Eden, the first gardener

explanation.surface: A woman wed countless men, among them an elderly gardener.
explanation.definitionFit: Madame is the French title for a married woman, the equivalent of Mrs.

clue.text: Protest over bishop — something happening at end of service

definitions.text: something happening at end of service

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above the next piece

parts.note: a demo is a protest march
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A protest about a bishop at the close of a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' suggests church, but means military service.
explanation.definitionFit: Demob, short for demobilisation, is release from the armed forces when service ends.

clue.text: One assesses resistance to watershed being abused

indicators.note: abused means mistreated, so the letters are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: Something resisting the misuse of a watershed.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder includes 'to' and 'being' as well as 'watershed'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Wheatstone bridge is an electrical circuit for measuring an unknown resistance.

clue.text: Female artificial in speech

indicators.note: in speech means as spoken, so the word sounds like another

parts.note: artificial means made by people, man-made

explanation.surface: A woman who is fake when she talks.
explanation.definitionFit: A maid is a girl or young woman, and also a female servant.

clue.text: Go on social network, head buried

indicators.note: with its head buried, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: Twitter is a social network, now called X

explanation.surface: Someone goes online to a social network with their head down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go on' looks like 'go onto', but means talk on and on.
explanation.definitionFit: To witter is British informal for chattering at length about trivial things.

clue.text: A bill, say, for a high-ranking Turkish official

parts.note: a tab is a bill, as in a bar tab
e.g. means for example, as 'say' does

explanation.surface: A bill presented for a senior Turkish official.
explanation.definitionFit: An atabeg was a hereditary governor or ruler in Seljuk Turkish lands.
